requirements.requirement: A seven-cell honeycomb (centre cell plus six around it)
Stands on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet
requirements.evidence: 6 stud spikes facing down, one at each of the six junctions around the centre cell. That is more than the three asked for. The check found no rule issues and no mesh collisions.

finish.summary: I built a seven-cell honeycomb: a centre base with six full hex bases around it, all on one storey. Six stud spikes face down as feet, one at each of the six points where three cells meet around the centre. The configurator only offered those inner junctions, so the feet are all under the inner ring and none sit at the outer rim. I also capped the open outer faces (18 solid end caps) and bolted the joints (12 joint bolts). That makes 31 parts in all, and the estimate is about 2.3 kg of filament. The checks found no rule issues and no mesh collisions.

lines.label: M6 brass heat-set insert, 7.6 mm (initeq M6-1.0 Short)
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
